This implements the four tasks in `simulation.Rmd`. The original pseudocode is
unchanged. Run the chunks in order, or render this document. Dependencies are
`here` and `ggplot2`; `parallel` is included with R.

# Task 1: Generate two datasets

Both datasets share the same 50 rows of predictors. The CSV files include an
explicit `intercept` column, but the fitting formula uses only `x1` through `x5`:
R adds the model intercept automatically. Files use the existing `Data/` folder.

The continuous model retains the original coefficients. The binary model uses
the smaller coefficients agreed upon after the original values produced an
imbalanced outcome and a nonconvergent logistic fit.

```{r}
#| label: simulate-data
here::i_am("R/simulation.qmd")
set.seed(648)

n <- 50L
X <- cbind(
  intercept = rep(1, n),
  x1 = rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1),
  x2 = rnorm(n, mean = 5, sd = 5),
  x3 = rpois(n, lambda = 3),
  x4 = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.3),
  x5 = runif(n, min = 0, max = 10)
)

beta_cont <- c(1, 1, -0.5, 2, -2, 0.5)
beta_binary <- c(-1, 0.3, -0.1, 0.3, -0.5, 0.1)

cont <- data.frame(X, Y = drop(X %*% beta_cont) + rnorm(n, 0, 1))
p <- plogis(drop(X %*% beta_binary))
binary <- data.frame(X, Y = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = p))

dir.create(here::here("Data"), showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(cont, here::here("Data", "cont.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(binary, here::here("Data", "binary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Read the saved datasets for the examples below.
cont <- read.csv(here::here("Data", "cont.csv"))
binary <- read.csv(here::here("Data", "binary.csv"))
table(binary$Y)
```

# Task 2: Fit one model and return its coefficients

`family` is a function such as `gaussian` or `binomial`; `link` is a string such
as `"identity"` or `"logit"`. `model.frame()` collects the formula variables,
then `model.matrix()` and `model.response()` extract the design and outcome.
The arguments to `glm.fit()` are lowercase `x` and `y`.

```{r}
#| label: fit-function
#' Fit a GLM and retain only its named coefficient vector.
#' @param formula A model formula with a single numeric response.
#' @param data A data frame containing the formula variables.
#' @param family A GLM family function, for example gaussian or binomial.
#' @param link A character string naming the link.
#' @return A named numeric coefficient vector.
fit_fun <- function(formula, data, family = gaussian, link = "identity") {
  if (!is.function(family)) {
    stop("family must be a function, such as gaussian or binomial.")
  }
  if (!is.character(link) || length(link) != 1L || is.na(link)) {
    stop("link must be one string, such as 'identity' or 'logit'.")
  }

  mf <- stats::model.frame(formula, data = data, na.action = stats::na.fail)
  X <- stats::model.matrix(attr(mf, "terms"), data = mf)
  y <- stats::model.response(mf)
  if (!is.numeric(y) || !is.null(dim(y))) {
    stop("Use a single numeric response (0/1 for the binary example).")
  }
  if (any(!is.finite(X)) || any(!is.finite(y))) {
    stop("Model variables must be finite and contain no missing values.")
  }

  fit <- stats::glm.fit(x = X, y = y, family = family(link = link))
  if (!isTRUE(fit$converged)) {
    stop("The GLM did not converge; inspect the data and model specification.")
  }
  if (fit$rank < ncol(X) || any(!is.finite(fit$coefficients))) {
    stop("The model has coefficients that cannot be estimated uniquely.")
  }
  fit$coefficients
}
```

# Task 3: Predict the omitted rows and create an S3 result

The coefficient matrix has one row per omitted observation and one column per
model coefficient. The prediction for row `i` uses only row `i` of that matrix:
`sum(X[i, ] * beta[i, ])`. Column names align the coefficients with the design.

The inverse link converts the linear predictor to the response scale. This is
determined by the chosen family and link, regardless of the distributions of
the predictors. For the binary example, predictions are probabilities.

Here `bias` follows the pseudocode's direction: **predicted minus observed**.
These are individual prediction errors, rather than an estimate of simulation
bias across repeated datasets. MAE and RMSE use all rows; failed fits stop the
calculation rather than silently removing observations.

```{r}
#| label: predictions-and-s3
#' Make row-wise LOO predictions and assemble a result object.
#' @param beta Matrix whose ith row contains coefficients fitted without row i.
#' @param dat The original data frame, in its original row order.
#' @param formula The formula used in every fit.
#' @param family The family function used in every fit.
#' @param link The link string used in every fit.
#' @return An object of class loo_results.
predict_fun <- function(beta, dat, formula, family = gaussian,
                        link = "identity") {
  mf <- stats::model.frame(formula, data = dat, na.action = stats::na.fail)
  X <- stats::model.matrix(attr(mf, "terms"), data = mf)
  y <- stats::model.response(mf)

  if (!is.matrix(beta) || nrow(beta) != nrow(X) ||
      ncol(beta) != ncol(X) ||
      !setequal(colnames(beta), colnames(X))) {
    stop("beta must have one row per observation and matching model columns.")
  }
  beta <- beta[, colnames(X), drop = FALSE]
  family_spec <- family(link = link)
  eta <- rowSums(X * beta)
  pred <- family_spec$linkinv(eta)
  if (any(!is.finite(pred))) {
    stop("The model produced non-finite predictions.")
  }
  bias <- pred - y

  results <- list(
    formula = formula,
    family = family_spec,
    nrow = nrow(dat),
    ncol = ncol(dat),
    coefficients = beta,
    observed = y,
    predicted = pred,
    bias = bias,
    mae = mean(abs(bias)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean(bias^2))
  )
  class(results) <- "loo_results"
  results
}

#' @param x A loo_results object.
#' @param ... Additional method arguments.
#' @return The input object, invisibly.
print.loo_results <- function(x, ...) {
  cat("Leave-one-out prediction metrics\n")
  cat(sprintf("MAE:  %.6f\nRMSE: %.6f\n", x$mae, x$rmse))
  invisible(x)
}

#' @param object A loo_results object.
#' @param ... Additional method arguments.
#' @return The input object, invisibly, after displaying its summary.
summary.loo_results <- function(object, ...) {
  cat("Formula:", paste(deparse(object$formula), collapse = " "), "\n")
  cat("Data:", object$nrow, "rows and", object$ncol, "columns\n")
  cat("Family:", object$family$family,
      "| Link:", object$family$link, "\n")
  print(object)
  invisible(object)
}

# A custom S3 method needs a generic with the matching name.
#' @param x A result object.
#' @param ... Additional method arguments.
#' @return The dispatched plot.
plot_bias <- function(x, ...) {
  UseMethod("plot_bias")
}

#' @param x A loo_results object.
#' @param bins Number of histogram bins.
#' @param ... Reserved for additional arguments.
#' @return A ggplot histogram of predicted minus observed errors.
plot_bias.loo_results <- function(x, bins = 10L, ...) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(bias = x$bias), ggplot2::aes(x = bias)) +
    ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = bins, color = "white", fill = "steelblue") +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "LOO prediction errors",
      x = "Predicted - observed", y = "Count"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
}
```

# Task 4: Run LOO, using four workers by default

`data[-i, , drop = FALSE]` removes row `i` and keeps a data frame. `parLapplyLB()`
assigns rows dynamically to available workers; it does not guarantee exactly
equal work per worker. Its returned list stays in the input row order.
`on.exit()` ensures that the cluster closes even if a fit fails.

```{r}
#| label: run-loo
#' Run one-row-at-a-time LOO validation.
#' @param formula A model formula.
#' @param data The complete data frame.
#' @param family A family function, for example gaussian or binomial.
#' @param link A link string.
#' @param workers Number of PSOCK workers; 1 runs serially for checking.
#' @return An object of class loo_results.
run_loo <- function(formula, data, family = gaussian, link = "identity",
                    workers = 4L) {
  if (!is.data.frame(data) || nrow(data) < 3L) {
    stop("data must be a data frame with at least three rows.")
  }
  if (!is.numeric(workers) || length(workers) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(workers) || workers < 1 || workers != floor(workers)) {
    stop("workers must be a positive integer.")
  }

  indices <- seq_len(nrow(data))
  if (workers == 1L) {
    res <- lapply(indices, function(i) {
      fit_fun(formula, data[-i, , drop = FALSE], family, link)
    })
  } else {
    cl <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(as.integer(workers))
    on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cl), add = TRUE)
    parallel::clusterExport(
      cl, c("fit_fun", "formula", "data", "family", "link"),
      envir = environment()
    )
    res <- parallel::parLapplyLB(cl, indices, function(i) {
      fit_fun(formula, data[-i, , drop = FALSE], family, link)
    })
  }

  # Avoid silently combining coefficient vectors with different model columns.
  same_columns <- vapply(res, function(b) {
    identical(names(b), names(res[[1L]]))
  }, logical(1))
  if (!all(same_columns)) {
    stop("The model columns changed between LOO fits.")
  }
  beta <- do.call(rbind, res)
  predict_fun(beta, data, formula, family, link)
}
```

# Examples

These examples use numeric predictors, a numeric response, ordinary unweighted
GLMs, and no missing data. Predictors with data-dependent transformations, new
factor levels, offsets, or weights require additional handling and are outside
this example's scope. Convergence warnings remain visible for inspection.

```{r}
#| label: examples
model_formula <- Y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5

cont_result <- run_loo(model_formula, cont, gaussian, "identity")
binary_result <- run_loo(model_formula, binary, binomial, "logit")

print(cont_result)
summary(binary_result)
plot_bias(cont_result)
plot_bias(binary_result)
```

# Check the implementation

Compare serial and parallel coefficients and predictions, then independently
fit each omitted-row model with `glm()` and predict that row using
`type = "response"`. Recalculate the metrics and check the probability range.

```{r}
#| label: verification
cont_serial <- run_loo(model_formula, cont, gaussian, "identity", workers = 1L)
binary_serial <- run_loo(model_formula, binary, binomial, "logit", workers = 1L)

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(cont_result, cont_serial)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(binary_result, binary_serial))
)

for (kind in c("continuous", "binary")) {
  dat <- if (kind == "continuous") cont else binary
  result <- if (kind == "continuous") cont_result else binary_result
  family_spec <- if (kind == "continuous") gaussian("identity") else binomial("logit")

  reference <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(dat)), function(i) {
    fit <- stats::glm(model_formula, data = dat[-i, , drop = FALSE],
                      family = family_spec)
    as.numeric(stats::predict(fit, newdata = dat[i, , drop = FALSE],
                              type = "response"))
  }, numeric(1))

  stopifnot(
    length(result$predicted) == nrow(dat),
    isTRUE(all.equal(result$predicted, reference, check.attributes = FALSE)),
    isTRUE(all.equal(result$mae, mean(abs(reference - dat$Y)))),
    isTRUE(all.equal(result$rmse, sqrt(mean((reference - dat$Y)^2))))
  )
}
stopifnot(all(binary_result$predicted >= 0 & binary_result$predicted <= 1))
cat("All serial/parallel, direct-prediction, and metric checks passed.\n")
```
